title: Tokens and Training
summary: Long prompts mean more time and cost — shorten them before switching models.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What will you understand?** **Why** do **long prompts** take **more time** and **cost more** — and how does this affect **every prompt** you write?
- **Why now?** When you build an **AI feature** in your product — **every character** counts. **Shortening** is not a luxury — it’s **design**.
- **What after the lesson?** You will compare a **short prompt** and a **long prompt** and explain **what you will remove**.

sections.heading: Tension — Long Prompt — Slow or Expensive Response
sections.subtitle: Long Prompt — Slow or Expensive Response
sections.contentMarkdown:
- You wrote a **long introduction** and said "please" and "my friend" — and the response came **after a while**, or your **API bill** increased.
- It’s not necessarily that the **model** is "slow" — often **you** sent **too much** text.
- In **Lovable** or **Cursor**: the larger the **context** — the slower the **building and response**. **Rule:** **Shorten** — **you gain**.

sections.heading: Core Idea — Long Inputs and Outputs = More Time and Cost
sections.subtitle: Long Inputs and Outputs = More Time and Cost
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **AI** breaks your text into **small pieces (tokens)** — a **token** = a word or **part** of it.
- **Every token** in **input** and **every token** in **response** counts: **speed**, **cost**, **memory limit**.
- When you **build**: **long system prompt** + **user context** + **conversation history** = **bill and time**. **Shorten** what is **not necessary**.
- **Shorten the prompt**, **define what’s needed**, **remove introductions** — often **the same result** at a **lower cost**.

sections.heading: Comparison — Same Prompt · Two Formulations
sections.subtitle: Same Prompt · Two Formulations
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Fluff and Introductions | Direct |
|-------------|--------|
| "My AI friend, please can you help me with a simple task, which is to summarize this article..." — **the entire introduction** is a **waste of tokens** | "**Summarize the article** in **3 points**." — **a short sentence**, **faster response**, **lower cost**, **and the same result** |

sections.heading: Glossary — Two Terms to Start
sections.subtitle: Two Terms to Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| **Token** | **A small piece** of text — a **word** or **part** of it. **AI** counts it **in and out** | "Hello" can be **one token** or **two** depending on **language** and **model** |
| **Training** | **A stage** before you **use** the model — it learns from a **huge amount** of texts. **You** **do not** train it; you just **use** it | **ChatGPT** "**trains**" on internet texts — **you** just **write a prompt** |

sections.heading: Diagram Block (Intent)
sections.contentMarkdown:
**From prompt to response — every step counts** (ID: `ai-summarization-flow`):

**Prompt → Tokenization → Model → Response**

Every step in the flow **consumes tokens**. When you **shorten the prompt** — you **shorten the entire flow**.

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Check
sections.subtitle: Quick Check
sections.contentMarkdown:
> **Quiz key (unchanged):** correctIndex: 1

**Question:** If the **AI** is **slow** to respond — what is the **first thing** you try?

Change the model** immediately.**
**Shorten your prompt** and remove **excess introductions**.
Wait** and try again **without changes.

**Explanation:** **Shortening the prompt** is the fastest **improvement** — **before** changing **tools** or **models**.

sections.heading: Mission — Short vs Long Prompt — What Will You Remove?
sections.subtitle: Short vs Long Prompt — What Will You Remove?
sections.contentMarkdown:
**The task:** **Same prompt** in two formulations: **one long** and **one short**. **10 minutes** is enough.

**Delivery:**

1. **The long prompt** (write or copy it)
2. **The short prompt** (same request, **fewer words**)
3. **What did you remove** from the long version? (introductions, repetition, unnecessary details)
4. If the **feature** in your product will work **100 times/day** — what will **shortening** save you?

**Evaluation Criteria:**

| Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Real Comparison | 60% | Both prompts **for the same request**; the **shorter** one is **actually** shorter |
| Shortening Analysis | 40% | You identified **what** was removed **and why**; **linked** it to **cost** or **speed** in the product |

sections.contentMarkdown:
